file_name: Nicklas et al. - 2020 - Development and Modification of a Mobile Health Program to Promote Postpartum Weight Loss in Women a.txt

barriers.description: Developing and testing the app only on the iPhone platform limited the pool of participants and affected sample demographics and generalizability.
barriers.justification: This platform choice constrained recruitment and the team's ability to manage a representative user understanding and understand the broader context of use across device ecosystems.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We developed and tested the Fit After Baby app on an iPhone Operating System platform. This affected the demographics and economic status of the recruited participants, which may thereby affect generalizability. We are currently developing an Android version of the Fit After Baby app and will be able to use both versions for future studies.

barriers.description: Participant availability and competing demands during the postpartum period reduced consistent engagement in online groups and attendance at in-person focus groups.
barriers.justification: Irregular participation hindered the designers' ability to facilitate sustained user involvement, gather iterative feedback each week, and reliably evaluate and integrate findings across rounds.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Consistent with the demands of women during this very challenging postpartum period, all participants did not contribute to the online focus group every week. Although we attempted to conduct 2 in-person focus groups, we had several women who were unable to attend at the last minute and had to convert the 2 focus groups to 2-person group interviews.

barriers.description: Reliance on the external MyFitnessPal app for diet tracking created usability friction (app switching) that frustrated participants and reduced tracking adherence.
barriers.justification: This third-party integration issue limited the designers' ability to obtain consistent diet-tracking data and to evaluate and understand real user behavior in context, forcing changes to tracking frequency and tool choices.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Participants expressed some frustration with tracking of dietary intake. Participants had to download the MyFitnessPal app and open the app to record food and drink, and they complained that it was difficult to switch back and forth between apps.

barriers.description: Problems syncing steps from participants' Fitbit devices to the Fit After Baby app and the limitations of clip-style Fitbits impaired reliable activity tracking.
barriers.justification: Unreliable third-party device syncing constrained the team's ability to evaluate physical activity, provide targeted coaching, and understand participants' usage, requiring hardware changes for later iterations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: They complained that their steps were not always syncing qith the Fit AFter Baby app. The majority of participants stated that they would have preferred a wrist band Fitbit, so we transitioned to this for the final version of the program. The wrist Fitbit (Fitbit Flex 2) is also waterproof, so we felt that this would encourage adherence since some participants told us they forgot to remove the clip Fitbits from their clothes before washing them.
